page: Amazon Web Services c6in.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory configuration includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration support is present via AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI instructions, alongside hardware cryptographic engines including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include local NVMe storage and relies entirely on external Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes. It also contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs. Networking capabilities are an essential differentiator for the c6in series, offering a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In synthetic and platform benchmarks, the system registered 15,444.96 in stress-ng multi-core tests, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,346.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 21,375.14. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 91.31 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measured 49.5 GB/sec.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid throughput for network and compute routines, achieving 21.88 GB/sec in static web serving tests and 15.84 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Clang compilation scored 14,601.0, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 45.07 GB/sec. However, LLM inference evaluations show limits for memory-intensive computations: small 135M parameter models process prompts at 943.66 tokens per second, but 7B parameter prompt processing falls to 31.96 tokens per second, falling into the bottom 25th percentile due to the lack of dedicated acceleration and standard DDR4 bandwidth.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the c6in.4xlarge balances high dedicated vCPU density with robust 25 Gbps network bandwidth, avoiding the cost overhead of attached local SSD arrays when workloads do not require scratch disk space. The platform is technically suited for network-intensive compute tasks, distributed caching tiers, CI/CD compilation runners, static web serving clusters, and batch data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor and the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it delivers a focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. It includes no integrated GPU and no local instance storage, routing storage I/O externally while offering a high baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the instance produced 15.84 million Redis SET operations per second, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,346.0, and static web serving throughput of 21.88 GB/sec. Given its high network capacity and balanced compute density, the instance fits network-bound compute workloads, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, and distributed batch processing.
